newsitem.title: UK: Tesco slashes cost of Levi jeans.
newsitem.headline: Tesco slashes cost of Levi jeans.

text.p: British supermarket group Tesco Plc has triggered an investigation at jeans maker Levi Strauss & Co after launching sales of the company's jeans at cut prices, company sources said on Thursday.
"It has raised several issues that we are investigating," a spokeswoman for Levi Strauss, whose world-famous jeans are favourites with a host of international celebrities, told Reuters.
Tesco started selling the jeans at 150 of its 500 or so stores on March 24 at 30 pounds ($48.85) a pair compared with prices of 50 pounds or above often charged by designated Levi stockists.
"They have been selling extremely well and in some stores we have already sold out...we are trying to sort out emergency deliveries," a spokeswoman for Tesco said.
Tesco said it had sourced thousands of pairs of the men's jeans "unofficially direct from a Levi's factory".

Levi Strauss, which is the leader in Britain's 1.2 billion pound a year denim market and thus very keen on protecting and promoting its brand, did not know where Tesco had bought the jeans, the spokeswoman said. "That's a question for Tesco," she said.
Levi Strauss had talks with Tesco a year ago on the possibility of the supermarket stocking its jeans, she added, but Tesco failed to meet the company's quality and objectives criteria.
But she added that Levi Strauss had said it could be approached again if circumstances changed.
Tesco said Levi Strauss had refused to supply "on the grounds that Tesco was an inappropriate outlet".
Newspaper reports on the row suggested Levi Strauss objected to its jeans being sold next to groceries.
Levi Strauss said it advised customers to buy from authorised stockists where staff were specially trained and a full range was stocked.
The spokeswoman added that there are department stores which have grocery areas which are authorised stockists, but the clothing area is clearly segmented.

Supermarkets in Britain have targeted a range of products in the past to bring down prices, with value-for-money ASDA managing to help break fixed prices on books and currently challenging price constraints on over-the-counter medicines.
ASDA said it had no plans, however, to stock cut price Levi jeans.
"We are too busy selling our own George range of jeans," a spokesman said.
ASDA sells its George men's jeans at 16.99 pounds and 19.99 pounds per pair.
